s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers with systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
Enlargement of the tongue leading to difficulty with mastication
Numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the skin
Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum
Low serum zinc level
Subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands on biopsy
key_facts: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
3-month history of tongue enlargement
3-month history of numbness without weakness of the distal lower limbs
Difficulty with mastication due to tongue enlargement
Restricted mobility requiring diapers
History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma
Anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Conservative management with transfusions
Folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements due to deficiencies
Platelet count: 171 × 10^3/μL
Prothrombin time: 11.7 seconds
Activated partial thromboplastin time: 36.0 seconds
Serum zinc: 34.4 μg/dL
Biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands
Negative direct immunofluorescence test
Negative Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands

shortlist.label: Primary amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands, and clinical presentation of progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers

shortlist.label: Acquired Cutaneous Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers, and history of multiple myeloma

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: History of multiple myeloma and clinical presentation of progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers

shortlist.label: Bullous amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy findings of subepidermal blister with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and eosinophilic bands, and clinical presentation of progressive painful skin lesions and ulcers

raw.rationale: The patient's history of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and the presence of subepidermal blisters with eosinophilic bands showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining are consistent with amyloidosis associated with multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Primary amyloidosis
rejected.why: While primary amyloidosis can present with similar symptoms, the patient's history of multiple myeloma makes multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acquired Cutaneous Amyloidosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with macular amyloidosis or lichen amyloidosis, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation of blisters and ulcers.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: The negative direct immunofluorescence test and the presence of eosinophilic bands with apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining make paraneoplastic pemphigus less likely.

rejected.label: Bullous amyloidosis
rejected.why: While bullous amyloidosis can present with blisters, the patient's history of multiple myeloma and the specific biopsy findings make multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis a more specific diagnosis.
